summary:
The repo has a consistent, hand-rolled house pattern for AI calls: three env-overridable model ids in lib/ai-models.ts, direct `@anthropic-ai/sdk` dynamic imports inside each route, JSON-by-hand-parse (never tool use), and cost logged to `ai_cost_log` via lib/ai-cost.ts `recordCost`. Cheapest tier already in production use is HAIKU_MODEL = `claude-haiku-4-5` ($1 in / $5 out per 1M in the rate card), and it is what triage and all three wizards already run on.

For the founder's ask, three findings matter most. First, `ai_triage_request` cannot be reused as-is for a not-yet-created request: it loads the request from D1 by `[id]` and 404s if absent, and its org access scoping keys off the loaded row. The prompt-building and parsing below that are pure and portable but live inline in the route, unexported. Second, triage suggests only assignee, priority, track and a reason — it does not suggest a due date, estimated hours, or category (category is an input to it, not an output). Third, and most consequential for "nothing when confidence is low": there is no confidence concept anywhere in the repo, and triage does the exact opposite of what the founder wants — `parseSuggestion` coerces a missing or unparseable priority/track to `'standard'`/`'small'` and substitutes a canned sentence for a missing reason, so a thin-context answer comes back looking exactly as confident as a good one.

The closest existing precedent to the ask is not AI at all: lib/request-size-suggestion.ts is a pure, deterministic suggester that returns the size plus every string the dialog renders, consumed by new-request-dialog.tsx. Also note there is a live, admin-authed, zero-consumer endpoint at app/api/admin/ai/ai/suggest whose response shape (estimatedHours, suggestedPriority, steps, summary) is nearly exactly the founder's ask, currently implemented as pure keyword heuristics with a "wire to Claude API when ready" comment.
facts: Model tiers are centralised and env-overridable in C:\Users\Work\Projects\tahi-dashboard\lib\ai-models.ts:20-22 — OPUS_MODEL='claude-opus-4-8' (ANTHROPIC_OPUS_MODEL), SONNET_MODEL='claude-sonnet-5' (ANTHROPIC_SONNET_MODEL), HAIKU_MODEL='claude-haiku-4-5' (ANTHROPIC_HAIKU_MODEL). The file's rationale is that a model bump used to be a 17-file find-replace.

CHEAPEST TIER ALREADY IN USE: HAIKU_MODEL / 'claude-haiku-4-5', priced at $1.00 in / $5.00 out per 1M tokens in lib/ai-cost.ts:34. It backs triage, the admin request wizard, the portal request wizard, the task wizard and content send-to-staci. Sonnet 5 is $2/$10 (lib/ai-cost.ts:31), Opus 4.8 is $5/$25 (lib/ai-cost.ts:30).
lib/ai-models.ts:18-19 notes Opus 4.8 shipped a 'Fast Mode at 1/3 cost' marked 'TBD: wire up at call sites that don't need the full latency budget' — it is not wired anywhere.

Routes under app/api/admin/ai/ are: briefing/ (+ briefing/cron), request-wizard/, suggest/, task-wizard/. There is NO app/api/admin/ai/triage — triage lives at app/api/admin/requests/[id]/triage/route.ts. Lead enrichment lives at app/api/admin/leads/[id]/enrich/route.ts, draft-reply at app/api/admin/requests/[id]/draft-reply/route.ts.

app/api/admin/ai/suggest/route.ts is 128 lines of PURE KEYWORD HEURISTICS with no model call at all; its docstring at line 24 says 'Currently returns heuristic-based mock data. Wire to Claude API when ready.' It returns {estimatedHours, suggestedPriority, suggestedSteps, summary} from a keyword match over title+description+category (lines 45-118). Grep across app/, components/, lib/ finds ZERO consumers — it is admin-authed dead code whose response shape is nearly exactly the founder's ask.

TRIAGE END TO END (app/api/admin/requests/[id]/triage/route.ts, 237 lines): POST-only, admin gate at :118-121, org access scoping via requireAccessToOrg at :147-148, roster query bounded to 50 rows at :161.

TRIAGE OUTPUT SHAPE (:33-45, :55-61): suggestedAssigneeId, suggestedPriority ('standard'|'high'), suggestedTrack ('small'|'large'), oneLineReason. It does NOT suggest a due date, estimated hours, or category. Category is an INPUT rendered into the prompt at :173, never an output.

TRIAGE PROMPT (:33-45) is a single const SYSTEM_PROMPT sent as a system array with cache_control ephemeral (:210-214) so repeat passes hit the prompt cache. Model HAIKU_MODEL, max_tokens 400 (:206-207). Prompt explicitly says 'Only reason from what the request actually says. Do not invent urgency or scope that is not there.' and 'OUTPUT: a single JSON object and nothing else.'

TRIAGE CANNOT BE REUSED FOR A NOT-YET-CREATED REQUEST: it selects the request from D1 by [id] at :127-140 and returns 404 at :142-144 if absent, then scopes on the loaded request.orgId at :147. Everything from :168 down (prompt assembly from title/category/type/orgName/description + roster, and parseSuggestion) is pure and portable but is inline in the route file and not exported.

TRIAGE HAS NO CONFIDENCE AND CANNOT ABSTAIN: parseSuggestion at :99-100 coerces anything that is not literally 'high' to 'standard' and anything not 'large' to 'small', and :110 substitutes the canned sentence 'Suggested routing based on the request contents.' when the reason is missing. A thin-context or malformed answer is therefore indistinguishable from a confident one. Only the assignee can come back null, and only because it is validated against the real roster at :97/:106.

TRIAGE LOGS NO COST: the route never imports or calls recordCost. Same for both request wizards and draft-reply. The ONLY request/task AI route that writes to ai_cost_log is the task wizard (app/api/admin/ai/task-wizard/route.ts:825-833, scope 'wizard', stage 'task_wizard' or 'task_wizard_document').

COST PLUMBING: lib/ai-cost.ts holds RATE_CARD (:27-50), pure estimateCostCents (:71-83) and recordCost (:88-104) which inserts into schema.aiCostLog. Table is defined at db/schema.ts:3363 ('ai_cost_log') with scope / scopeId / stage / provider / model / inputTokens / outputTokens / callUnits / estimatedUsdCents / note. The Scope union at lib/ai-cost.ts:56 already includes 'wizard', deliberately scoped apart from content spend.

SPEND CIRCUIT BREAKER exists only in the task wizard: WIZARD_DAILY_CAP_CENTS = 500 ($5/day) at app/api/admin/ai/task-wizard/route.ts:55, checked at :754-764 returning 429 with reason 'ai_rate_limited'. wizardSpendTodayCents (:625-637) returns null rather than 0 when D1 is unreachable, and null is deliberately treated as 'let the call through'.

SHARED WRAPPER lib/anthropic-cost.ts `claudeJson` (:79) is the richer client: per-draft cost cap (:84-89), one stricter 'JSON only' retry on parse failure (:176), 429/529 backoff honouring Retry-After with jitter and 5 attempts (:147-161), cache_control ephemeral system blocks (:110-118), and cache-token accounting summed into input (:138-145). It is used ONLY by the content pipeline — none of the request/task/triage AI routes use it.

DEGRADED FALLBACK (task wizard :737-744, request wizard :389-395, identical shape): if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is missing, production returns 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE and local dev returns 200 with handleDeterministic() (a regex/keyword draft) spread with DEGRADED = {degraded:true, reason:'ai_unavailable'} (task-wizard :128). The docstring at task-wizard :6-13 and :123-127 states the design intent: a 200 carrying a regex draft that the panel painted like a real answer was the failure mode being removed.

OTHER FAILURE PAYLOADS in the wizards: empty model text is a 502, not a fallback (task-wizard :838-840); upstream 429 maps to AI_RATE_LIMITED 429 (:874-876); an upstream 400 while a document was attached maps to 422 'ai_document_refused' (:880-887). By contrast triage and draft-reply have NO degraded path — missing key is a hard 500 (triage :163-166, draft-reply :132-134) and any API error is a 500.

JSON CONVENTION IS PARSE, NEVER TOOL USE. Triage strips fences then takes indexOf('{')..lastIndexOf('}') and JSON.parse in a try/catch (:75-90). Task wizard wraps a JSON array in <tasks> tags parsed by parseTasksFromResponse (:321). Request wizard uses parseRequestsFromResponse (:191). claudeJson uses stripCodeFences (:203) plus a caller-supplied parse. The ONLY tool use in the repo is Anthropic's server-side web search in lead enrichment: type 'web_search_20250305' at app/api/admin/leads/[id]/enrich/route.ts:435-437.

NO TIMEOUTS ANYWHERE: grep for AbortSignal / timeout: / maxRetries across app/api/admin/ai, app/api/admin/requests, app/api/admin/leads and lib/ai-*.ts returns nothing. All calls run on the SDK defaults. lib/anthropic-cost.ts:9 advertises 'timeout + error wrapping' but no timeout is actually configured — only the 429/529 backoff loop.

LEAD ENRICHMENT bypasses lib/ai-models.ts and hardcodes its own tiers: MODEL_FULL='claude-sonnet-5' and MODEL_SCORE='claude-haiku-4-5-20251001' at app/api/admin/leads/[id]/enrich/route.ts:37-38, max_tokens 2048 (:431), Sonnet+web_search for the full pass (:558) and Haiku score-only for the cheap daily cron (:520). Other hardcoders: cron/leads-ai:59, leads/rescore-all:35, leads/[id]/draft-reply:28, cron/ideation:49, cron/finance-anomaly-scan:267.

MCP EXPOSURE is a thin HTTP proxy, not a reimplementation. Tool declarations at workers/mcp-server/src/index.ts:1482 (ai_task_wizard), :1487 (ai_request_wizard), :1491 (ai_triage_request), :1494 (ai_draft_request_reply), plus enrich_lead at :880. Wizard dispatch via apiWrite at index.ts:2556-2559; triage and draft-reply dispatch at workers/mcp-server/src/request-tools.ts:196-199 returning {path:`/api/admin/requests/${requestId}/triage`, method:'POST', body:{}}. A parity test asserts that mapping at app/api/__tests__/mcp-request-tool-parity.test.ts:160.

AI CONTEXT INJECTION: lib/ai-context.ts loadAiContext(keys) (:63) pulls Docs Hub pages (icp / brandDna / tone / liamVoice / staciVoice / aiTells / services) resolved through the settings table, with a 5-minute in-memory cache (:56). It is additive — missing settings silently yield an empty string. draft-reply uses it (loadAiContext(['brandDna','tone'])) and passes each doc as its own cache_control block. Triage and the wizards do NOT use it.

CLOSEST EXISTING PRECEDENT TO THE ASK IS DETERMINISTIC, NOT AI: lib/request-size-suggestion.ts exports suggestRequestSize() (:71) returning {size, sizeLabel, chipLabel, helper, hint} — the suggestion plus every string the UI renders — driven by a 60-word brief threshold (:22) and a multi-day category list (:25), with a plan-capability override. Consumed at components/tahi/new-request-dialog.tsx:477-495, where clients see a chip with a Change link and the team sees a hint under the control.

THE REQUEST DUE DATE IS NOT ACTUALLY EMPTY TODAY: components/tahi/new-request-dialog.tsx:201 defines DUE_DATE_DEFAULT_DAYS = 7 and :382 initialises the field to isoDatePlusDays(7), reset again at :459 and :600. Any prediction would be replacing a blind constant rather than filling a blank.

ACCEPT/CLEAR UI PATTERN for suggestions already exists on request detail: the TriageSuggestion type at app/(dashboard)/requests/[id]/request-detail.tsx:456-463 is commented 'These are SUGGESTIONS only - nothing applies until the admin clicks Apply'; runTriage at :1304-1320; applyTriageAssignee at :1323-1327 clears the suggestion after applying, while applyTriagePriority at :1330-1333 does not clear it.

TARGET COLUMNS EXIST ON BOTH TABLES. requests (db/schema.ts): type (legacy small_task/large_task), size ('small'|'large'), category, status, priority (default 'standard'), estimatedHours (real), dueDate (text). tasks: priority (default 'standard'), assigneeId, assigneeType, dueDate, estimatedHours, with indexes idx_tasks_assignee and idx_tasks_due.

PORTAL TWIN EXISTS for the request wizard: app/api/portal/ai/request-wizard/route.ts, Haiku, max_tokens 1024 (:219-220), denies the Tahi admin org and derives orgId from Clerk (:377-380), and gates on requirePortalFeature(..., 'requests') (:384). Its docstring (:1-17) records the client-safe deltas: no hour estimates, no pricing, no track sizing, priority not surfaced, four client-facing categories only.
risks: The 'suggest nothing when confidence is low' requirement has no precedent in the codebase, and triage actively works against it: parseSuggestion (triage route :99-100, :110) coerces every unparseable field to a default and back-fills a canned reason. Reusing triage's parser for prediction would confidently fill every empty field on a two-word title. A prediction endpoint needs an explicit per-field null/abstain contract plus a confidence signal, both of which must be built from scratch.

ai_triage_request cannot be pointed at an uncreated request without refactoring: the route loads the row by [id] and 404s (:127-144), and its access check depends on the loaded orgId. The reusable part (prompt assembly + parse) is inline and unexported. Either extract it into lib/ or accept a second, near-duplicate prompt — the latter risks the two drifting on category rules and sizing language.

Triage does not produce the three fields the founder actually named: due date, estimated hours, and category. It produces track ('small'|'large'), which is adjacent to size but is not an hours estimate. Treating triage as 'already most of the way there' would overstate the starting point.

app/api/admin/ai/suggest is a live, admin-authed endpoint with zero consumers whose shape overlaps the ask almost exactly. Building a new prediction route beside it leaves two competing 'suggest' surfaces and a dead heuristic that future readers will assume is wired. Decide explicitly whether to fill it in or delete it.

Cost is invisible for triage, both request wizards, and draft-reply — none call recordCost. The only daily ceiling is WIZARD_DAILY_CAP_CENTS ($5) inside the task wizard. A prediction that fires on field blur, dialog open, or typing is precisely the runaway-loop shape that cap was written for, but it will not be covered unless the new route logs with scope 'wizard' and reads the same ledger.

lib/anthropic-cost.ts:30 restricts claudeJson's scope union to the content-pipeline scopes and omits 'wizard', even though lib/ai-cost.ts:56 includes it. Reusing claudeJson (the wrapper with retry, backoff and cost capping) for a wizard-scoped prediction requires widening that union — a one-line change that is easy to miss and will surface as a type error at build, not at review.

No AI call in the repo sets a timeout or AbortSignal; all run on SDK defaults. A prediction triggered by UI interaction can leave a dialog hanging with no ceiling. This is a new requirement class the existing routes never had to satisfy, since they are all explicit button presses.

The request dialog already blind-fills dueDate to today+7 (new-request-dialog.tsx:201, :382). 'Empty' needs a definition before implementation: untouched-default versus explicitly-cleared-by-the-operator. Predicting over a value the operator deliberately cleared would be the opposite of the ask.

CLAUDE.md rule 14 makes MCP parity mandatory, so a new prediction endpoint needs a matching ai_* tool in workers/mcp-server/src/index.ts plus a dispatch case, and there is an existing parity test (mcp-request-tool-parity.test.ts) that will need a corresponding entry.

Six routes hardcode model ids instead of importing lib/ai-models.ts (leads enrich, leads-ai cron, rescore-all, leads draft-reply, ideation cron, finance-anomaly-scan). A new route should import HAIKU_MODEL rather than copy a literal, or the env-override escape hatch the file was built for stops working for this feature too.

summary: Both creation forms are mapped. The admin/portal New Request dialog is one component (components/tahi/new-request-dialog.tsx) with an audience split on `isAdmin`, not two components: the portal client form IS the same dialog, so anything built there lands on both audiences at once. The New Task dialog (components/tahi/tasks/new-task-dialog.tsx) is a sibling with the same two-view shape (form / AI panel) but a different footer stack, a different FieldGroup, and no POST of its own. A prediction layer has a natural home in both: the request dialog already ships a pure heuristic suggester (lib/request-size-suggestion.ts) that guesses `size` from the brief plus category, renders it as a chip with a Change link, and writes it into form state only while the operator has not overridden. That is the exact pattern the founder is describing, generalised to due date / priority / hours / assignee. The main obstacles are that four fields are never actually empty (category, priority, size default on open, and the request due date is pre-filled +7 days), that neither dialog tracks which fields the operator has touched, that three existing writers (size effect, aiDraft prop, AI draft hand-off / template apply) all clobber fields unconditionally with no precedence rule, and that neither dialog holds any client history to predict from.

TASK FIELDGROUP ASYMMETRY: the task dialog's local FieldGroup (:168) takes {label, required, htmlFor, hint, children} and renders `hint` as a quiet line UNDER the field. It has no `after` slot beside the label, unlike the request dialog's FieldGroup (:2464). A shared per-field suggestion chip needs the task FieldGroup extended or a different placement.

TASK PRIMITIVES: SlideOver + SlideOver.Body (:418) + SlideOver.Footer (:645), SearchableSelect, SegmentedControl, TahiButton (:647 secondary Cancel, :655 primary 'Create task' with form="new-task-form" and `loading={submitting}`), useToast, LEVEL_ICON + checklistCountLabel from components/tahi/tasks/task-chips.tsx. Sparkles is used at :396 (SlideOver icon in AI view) and :670 (the AiAssistCard tile, label 'Draft with AI').

TASK QUICK-ADD is the repo's best existing UI precedent for showing a machine guess before committing: components/tahi/tasks/task-quick-add.tsx renders four live `Hint` chips (:35) for Client / Due / Priority / Level that tint when the parser found a token. Parsing is lib/tasks-quick-add.ts `parseQuickAdd` (grammar: `!urgent|!high|...`, weekday and relative dates, `@ClientName`), pure with an injectable `now`, and it returns `priority: null` to mean 'the user said nothing' so the caller falls back to the column default rather than writing 'standard' on purpose. tasks-content.tsx:614 posts title/type/orgId/dueDate/priority; the board column composer (:626) posts only title/status/orgId/type.

PORTAL CLIENT FORM SHARES EVERYTHING: app/(dashboard)/requests/page.tsx computes `isAdmin` from orgId and renders a single `<RequestList isAdmin={isAdmin} />`; there is no separate portal requests page or portal-only dialog. Inside AlignedRequestDialog `isClient = !isAdmin` (:353). Client differences: no client or brand picker, intake questions block, size rendered as a suggestion chip instead of the control, the three-option placement radiogroup instead of priority, no 'More details' (start date and est. hours are never offered to clients), and POST /api/portal/requests. A client's only genuinely blank fields on open are the brief (required) and nothing else.

SERVER VALIDATION DIFFERS BY ROUTE. app/api/portal/requests/route.ts hard-whitelists `type` against REQUEST_TYPES (:344) and `category` against REQUEST_CATEGORIES (:350), validates formResponses as JSON (:359), and runs a plan entitlement check that 400s `large_task` for a client with no multi-day track (:379-416). app/api/admin/requests/route.ts does NO whitelist on type or category at all: it writes `${type ?? 'small_task'}` and `${category ?? 'development'}` straight into the INSERT (:243-244), validating only clientOrgId + title (:159) and `status` against CREATABLE_STATUSES (:168).

app/api/admin/requests/route.ts:276 returns only `{ id }`, but the dialog's confirmation view reads `requestNumber`, `placement`, `queuePosition`, `planLabel` and `retainer` off the response (new-request-dialog.tsx:604-621). Admin confirmations therefore already render a null request number. The portal route returns the same bare `{ id }` when no placement was sent (app/api/portal/requests/route.ts:~555) and the richer payload only when one was.

HISTORY IS NOT IN EITHER DIALOG. The request dialog fetches only clients (`/api/admin/clients?status=active`, :418) and brands (`/api/admin/brands?orgId=`, :428). The per-client history a predictor would want already sits one level up in app/(dashboard)/requests/request-list.tsx:693 (SWR on `/api/admin/requests?status=all&limit=500`), and the row type at :90 carries category, priority, estimatedHours, startDate, dueDate, createdAt, orgId. Likewise the task dialog receives only option lists; app/(dashboard)/tasks/tasks-content.tsx holds the full task list (TASKS_KEY :94 = '/api/admin/tasks?status=all', TaskRow at lib/tasks-views.ts:25 carries priority, dueDate, estimatedHours, assigneeId, createdAt, completedAt). Either pass those down as props or add an endpoint.

TESTING CONVENTION: pure rules are exported from the component and unit-tested in Node with no DOM (components/tahi/__tests__/new-request-dialog.test.ts covers isoDatePlusDays, canSubmitRequest, submitBlockedReason, nextCategoryIndex, parseIntakeQuestions, toBriefHtml), and the interactive half is covered by e2e/requests-dialog.spec.ts. A suggestion engine should follow lib/request-size-suggestion.ts and live in lib/ as a pure module so tests never import a 'use client' file (that is the stated reason lib/task-wizard-drafts.ts exists).
risks: "If empty" barely applies as written. In the request dialog category defaults to 'development' (:378), priority to 'standard' (:380), size to 'small_task' (:377) and the due date is PRE-FILLED to today+7 (:382, DUE_DATE_DEFAULT_DAYS). In the task dialog priority defaults to 'standard' (:247). The only genuinely blank fields on open are title, brief/note, request start date, est. hours, task due date, assignee and checklist. Either the +7 default has to be dropped in favour of a suggestion, or the feature needs a per-field touched/dirty set (neither dialog tracks one today) so "empty" means "untouched by the operator".

Four writers will be fighting over the same state with no precedence rule. Today: the size suggestion effect (new-request-dialog.tsx:491, guarded by `suggestionShowing`), the `aiDraft` prop effect (:498), `handleDraftToForm` (:515), and on the task side `applyTemplate` (:260) plus `handleDraftToForm` (:321). The last three all overwrite unconditionally. Adding a fifth writer without an explicit precedence order (operator > template > AI draft > prediction) will produce flicker, clobber typed text, and re-suggest over a value the operator just cleared.

Neither dialog can see any history. The request dialog fetches clients and brands only; the task dialog receives option lists only. Predicting from "the client's history" requires either threading the parent page's already-loaded SWR data down as props (request-list.tsx:693, tasks-content.tsx:261) or adding a new endpoint, and a per-client aggregate endpoint hit on every dialog open is a cold-start cost on a Worker.

Two prediction implementations already exist and disagree. lib/request-size-suggestion.ts is live and pure; app/api/admin/ai/suggest/route.ts returns estimatedHours + suggestedPriority from a different keyword table and has zero consumers. Meanwhile ai-request-wizard.tsx's RequestDraft already carries priority and estimatedHours that new-request-dialog.tsx:515 discards. Shipping a third heuristic without reconciling these leaves the same field predicted three different ways.

Auto-filling `type` for a client can 400. app/api/portal/requests/route.ts:379-416 rejects `large_task` for a client whose plan has no multi-day track, with a customer-facing error. The dialog's `largeAllowed` (:373) is derived from `selectedClient?.planType` for admins and the `canUseLargeTrack` prop for clients, so a suggestion computed before the plan resolves (clientsLoading, or a sub-request whose parent org has not loaded) can post a size the server refuses.

Auto-filling client/request/level on a task can silently produce a repaired triple. lib/task-consistency.ts coerces, and app/api/admin/tasks/route.ts:264 coerces again server-side, so a bad suggestion does not 400: it lands as a different task than the one shown. Any predicted client, request or level must go through setTaskLevel/setTaskClient/setTaskRequest, and the UI must show the coerced result, not the suggestion.

There is no DatePicker primitive. Both dialogs use a native `<input type="date">` (new-request-dialog.tsx:858/:886/:921, new-task-dialog.tsx:543). A suggested date cannot be previewed inside a calendar popover; it has to be written into the input value or shown as an adjacent chip, and on iOS the native control gives no room for an inline badge.

The two dialogs' FieldGroups are not the same component and do not have the same slots: the request one has an `after` slot beside the label already carrying AiDraftChip and the due-date tooltip (:2464), the task one has only a `hint` line underneath (:168). A single shared "Suggested / Accept / Clear" affordance needs one of them changed, and the request dialog's hand-rolled footer vs the task dialog's SlideOver.Footer means the two cannot share a footer-level summary either.

The unreachable LegacyRequestDialog (new-request-dialog.tsx:1754-2460) still duplicates every field and is still typechecked and linted. Adding suggestion state to the aligned dialog only will read as drift, and the file is already 2644 lines before anything is added. Deleting the legacy half first (the file's own header comment says that is the plan once the flag flipped, and it has) is cheaper than maintaining the divergence.

Silent auto-fill on the client-facing portal changes what a client believes they asked for. The same component serves both audiences, so a due-date or size prediction shipped without an audience gate immediately appears on the portal, where the founder's own copy already says the date is "a target, not a promise" (DUE_DATE_TIP :181). Clients also never see priority or est. hours at all, so most of the suggestion surface is admin-only by construction and should be gated on `isAdmin` explicitly rather than by which fields happen to render.

CLAUDE.md rule 14 (MCP parity) means any new suggestion endpoint must also be exposed as a tool on workers/mcp-server/src/index.ts. A purely client-side heuristic in lib/ avoids this; a server route does not.

Board and column quick-adds are the highest-volume creation doors and have the thinnest context: requests quick-add posts only {clientOrgId, title, status} (request-list.tsx:1583) and the task column composer only {title, status, orgId, type} (tasks-content.tsx:626). If the suggestion layer lives inside the dialogs only, the doors that most need it will not get it; if it is pushed into the POST routes instead, the operator never sees or can correct the guess, which contradicts the "clearly marked suggestions the operator can accept, edit or clear" intent.

summary:
The grounding data for empty-field prediction exists and is queryable in one or two cheap D1 statements per client, but three of the five fields the founder named have weaker signal than expected. Requests carry no status history at all: deliveredAt (db/schema.ts:471, written only on the status PATCH at app/api/admin/requests/[id]/route.ts:230 and app/api/portal/requests/[id]/route.ts:277) and createdAt are the ONLY two lifecycle timestamps, so created-to-delivered is the only turnaround measurable, and auditLog never records a request status change. Tasks are better instrumented: completedAt is set on done and nulled when moved off (app/api/admin/tasks/[id]/route.ts:126). Priority is a two-value vocabulary on requests (standard | high, lib/request-vocabulary.ts:54) and three-value on tasks (lib/task-priorities.ts:15), so the distribution is nearly degenerate on requests. estimatedHours exists on both (db/schema.ts:454, :871) but is nullable and never written by any create path unless a human types it.

The indexes are wrong for the exact query wanted. Requests are indexed on org_id, status, assignee_id, track_id, request_number, parent_request_id and schedule_row_id only (db/schema.ts:480-486): NO index on category, created_at or delivered_at, so a per-client per-category 90-day median is an index scan on idx_requests_org then a filter. Acceptable at current volume (the same shape already runs in app/api/admin/reports/retainer-health/route.ts:112-136) but wants a composite (org_id, category, delivered_at) index if it moves onto the create hot path. Migration 0087 added idx_tasks_assignee and idx_tasks_due plus tasks.estimated_hours; migration 0086 is invoices.stripe_hosted_invoice_url + organisations.payment_terms and adds nothing task-related.

No SLA or default due date is stored anywhere. settings is a free key/value store (db/schema.ts:1589) and the fourteen keys the app actually uses contain nothing about turnaround. kanbanColumns holds label/statusValue/colour/position only (db/schema.ts:1647). The one SLA field that exists, requestForms.sla (db/schema.ts:1642, free text like '2 business days'), is writable from admin settings but silently DROPPED by the portal resolver's parseForm (app/api/portal/request-forms/route.ts:97-103), so the dialog can never read it. Fixing that one function is the cheapest path to a per-category, per-client, human-authored due-date rule needing no statistics.

The repo already has four ungrounded prediction implementations, and one silently pre-fills the exact field asked about: the new request dialog defaults dueDate to today+7 with no signal (components/tahi/new-request-dialog.tsx:201, :382), presented as a normal filled field. The new task dialog defaults dueDate to '' (components/tahi/tasks/new-task-dialog.tsx:248). The confidence-gate and only-fill-empty-fields mechanics are both already implemented elsewhere and should be reused.
facts: requests has no status-history table and no statusChangedAt column. The only lifecycle timestamps are createdAt/updatedAt (the `...timestamps` spread at db/schema.ts:478 -> :15-22) and deliveredAt (db/schema.ts:471). deliveredAt is written in exactly two places: app/api/admin/requests/[id]/route.ts:230 (`if (body.status === 'delivered') patch.deliveredAt = now`) and app/api/portal/requests/[id]/route.ts:277. Created-to-delivered days is therefore the ONLY turnaround the data supports; per-stage dwell time is unavailable.

auditLog (db/schema.ts:1567) is NOT a fallback status history. Only three files insert rows: lib/audit.ts:25, lib/contract-fully-signed-emails.ts:272, app/api/onboarding/complete/route.ts:226. logAudit callers are exclusively permissions / team / contact-role / copy-access / feature-visibility / portal-subscription routes. No request or task mutation writes an audit row.

Requests grounding columns, exact names and lines (db/schema.ts:422-486): orgId text('org_id') NOT NULL :424; trackId text('track_id') :425; type text('type') NOT NULL default 'small_task' (legacy size) :430; size text('size') default 'small' :433; category text('category') nullable :435; priority text('priority') NOT NULL default 'standard' :442; assigneeId text('assignee_id') -> teamMembers :443; estimatedHours real('estimated_hours') nullable :454; startDate text('start_date') :456; dueDate text('due_date') :457; isInternal integer boolean :466; formResponses text('form_responses') default '{}' :468; deliveredAt text('delivered_at') :471.

Tasks grounding columns (db/schema.ts:840-871): type text('type') NOT NULL is the LEVEL (client_task | internal_client_task | tahi_internal, see TASK_LEVELS in lib/tasks-views.ts) :843; orgId text('org_id') nullable, null for tahi_internal :845; priority :852; assigneeId text('assignee_id') + assigneeType :854; dueDate text('due_date') :856; completedAt text('completed_at') :857; trackId :862; requestId text('request_id') -> requests :866; estimatedHours real('estimated_hours') :871. Tasks have NO category column (lib/task-wizard-drafts.ts:20-22 states this explicitly).

tasks.completedAt is maintained both ways: app/api/admin/tasks/[id]/route.ts:126 sets it on done and back to null when the task leaves done, and app/api/admin/tasks/route.ts:322 sets it at create. Created-to-completed days per level is therefore a clean signal, unlike requests.

Request priority is a TWO-value vocabulary: REQUEST_PRIORITIES = ['standard','high'] (lib/request-vocabulary.ts:54, isRequestPriority :56). Task priority is THREE: TASK_PRIORITIES = ['standard','high','urgent'] (lib/task-priorities.ts:15). A priority distribution over requests is close to binary and useful mainly as an escalate flag, not a ranked prediction.

Request categories are a closed six-value list: REQUEST_CATEGORIES = ['design','development','content','strategy','admin','bug'] (lib/request-vocabulary.ts:76-83), mirrored by CATEGORY_TILES at components/tahi/new-request-dialog.tsx:173-180. The existing AI request wizard knows only FOUR of them ('design'|'development'|'content'|'strategy', app/api/admin/ai/request-wizard/route.ts:46 and :147), so it can never suggest admin or bug.

POST /api/admin/requests does NOT validate category, type or priority. It writes `${category ?? 'development'}` (app/api/admin/requests/route.ts:244) and `${priority ?? 'standard'}` (:247) straight into the row, and never sets the `size` column at all (the INSERT column list at :235-238 omits it). Only PATCH validates, via isRequestPriority at app/api/admin/requests/[id]/route.ts:233. Any autofill writing through the create path must validate itself.

No SLA or default-due-date is stored anywhere. The complete set of settings keys read via eq(schema.settings.key, ...) is: affiliates.reactivationDays, affiliates.reactivationEnabled, ai_briefing_latest, booking.google_cal_url, calls.preCallDigestEmail, content.publishCronEnabled, finance.yieldHoldings, leads.autoPromoteFromCalls, leads.defaultLeadOwnerId, leads.discoveryQuestionsTemplate, pipeline.defaultDealOwnerId, pipeline.forecastHorizonMonths, pipeline.nudgeSignatureHtml, plus invoicing.defaultChannel (lib/invoice-channel.ts:31). None concern turnaround.

kanbanColumns holds NOTHING about due dates or SLA: id, orgId, label, statusValue, colour, position, isDefault, timestamps (db/schema.ts:1647-1662). The seven default columns are hardcoded at app/api/admin/kanban-columns/route.ts:11-19 (Submitted, In Review, In Progress, Client Review, On Hold, Delivered, Cancelled).

requestForms.sla EXISTS and is the only human-authored turnaround signal in the schema: text('sla') at db/schema.ts:1642, documented as "Target turnaround label, e.g. '2 business days'", added by migration 0084 (app/api/admin/db/migrate/route.ts:1976). Writable at app/api/admin/forms/route.ts:103 and app/api/admin/forms/[id]/route.ts:47.

BUG blocking that signal: the portal form resolver drops sla. parseForm returns only { id, name, category, questions } (app/api/portal/request-forms/route.ts:97-103), and the dialog reads only `data.form?.questions` (components/tahi/new-request-dialog.tsx:404-408). requestForms.audience ('all_clients'|'retainer_clients'|'internal_only', db/schema.ts:1640) and description (:1638) are also dropped. The four-step resolution ladder (org+category > org global > category global > global default) is implemented at app/api/portal/request-forms/route.ts:28-71 and indexed by idx_request_forms_org_cat (org_id, category) and idx_request_forms_default.

The new request dialog ALREADY silently autofills a due date with zero grounding: DUE_DATE_DEFAULT_DAYS = 7 (components/tahi/new-request-dialog.tsx:201), applied at useState :382, on reset :459 and on save-another :600, via isoDatePlusDays (:195, local-calendar-safe not UTC). It renders as an ordinary filled date input, not a suggestion. The new task dialog by contrast leaves dueDate empty (components/tahi/tasks/new-task-dialog.tsx:248).

Four ungrounded predictors already exist and none reads the database: (1) app/api/admin/ai/suggest/route.ts, a pure keyword heuristic returning estimatedHours/suggestedPriority/suggestedSteps/summary, is DEAD CODE (no caller anywhere in app/, components/, lib/ or workers/) and emits `priority: 'urgent'` at :45 and :64 which requests cannot store. (2) lib/request-size-suggestion.ts suggests small/large from brief word count > 60 (BRIEF_WORD_THRESHOLD) and category in ['development','strategy'], with a plan override; wired into the dialog at :481-495. (3) app/api/admin/ai/request-wizard/route.ts:262-270 holds a hardcoded estimateHours table {design 8/32, development 12/46, content 6/18, strategy 6/23} plus detectCategory/detectType/detectPriority keyword tables at :228-258, and produces estimatedHours and priority but NEVER a dueDate. (4) lib/tasks-quick-add.ts parses due date, priority, client and level from one line of natural language and deliberately returns `priority: null` when the user said nothing so the caller falls back to the column default rather than writing 'standard' on purpose (:32-34).

The closest existing precedent is POST /api/admin/requests/[id]/triage (app/api/admin/requests/[id]/triage/route.ts, 237 lines). It reads title/category/type/description + org name + the team roster (limit 50, :150-161), asks Haiku, and returns suggestedAssigneeId/suggestedPriority/suggestedTrack/oneLineReason. It never mutates, validates the assignee id against the real roster so a hallucinated id becomes null (:98-100), and caches the system prompt (:207-211). Its limits: it runs POST-create on an existing request only, has no dueDate or estimatedHours output, and passes ZERO historical data into the prompt.

The only-fill-empty-fields mechanic is already implemented for leads: workers/mcp-server/src/index.ts:2113-2132 (`apply_lead_ai_suggestions`) patches name/email/jobTitle/company/website only `if (suggested.X && isEmpty(lead.X))` and returns `{ applied: 0 }` when everything is already filled. The same shape works verbatim for requests and tasks.

The confidence gate is also already implemented: lib/calculator/compute.ts:57-64 defines a plain JS median() returning null on an empty cohort, and :176-190 turns an empty cohort into the explicit verdict 'no_benchmark' rather than a made-up number. D1/SQLite has NO percentile or median function, so the median must be computed this way; there is no NTILE or percentile usage anywhere in the repo.

The one or two cheap D1 statements are proven in this shape. app/api/admin/reports/retainer-health/route.ts:112-136 runs three grouped-per-org COUNTs over requests with `gte(requests.createdAt, d90)` cutoffs inside a single Promise.all. app/api/admin/reports/overview/route.ts:57-66 proves julianday() arithmetic works on D1: `AVG(julianday(requests.delivered_at) - julianday(requests.created_at))` guarded by delivered_at IS NOT NULL, created_at IS NOT NULL and a `>= 0` sanity filter. For a median rather than a mean, select the raw `julianday(delivered_at) - julianday(created_at)` deltas for the org under a bounded LIMIT and take the median in JS with the compute.ts helper.

lib/track-stats.ts already computes the turnaround statistic, pure and unit-tested (lib/track-stats.test.ts): deliveredInWindow() filters by a windowDays cutoff (default 30) and trackDeliveredStats() returns { count, avgTurnaroundDays } with avgTurnaroundDays = null when the window is empty and Math.max(1, ...) as a floor. It is a mean not a median, and its window default is 30 days not 90.

Indexes on requests (db/schema.ts:480-486, created in drizzle/migrations/0000_equal_mojo.sql:326-329, 0003_married_molecule_man.sql:97 and app/api/admin/db/migrate/route.ts:162): org_id, status, assignee_id, track_id, request_number, parent_request_id, schedule_row_id. There is NO index on category, created_at, delivered_at, due_date, or org_id+category. A per-client per-category 90-day cohort scans idx_requests_org then filters.

Indexes on tasks (db/schema.ts:873-882): org_id, type, status, track_id, request_id, schedule_row_id, plus assignee_id and due_date added by migration 0087 (drizzle/migrations/0087_task_estimate_and_indexes.sql:16-17, mirrored at app/api/admin/db/migrate/route.ts:2019-2020). There is NO index on completed_at or created_at, so 'median created-to-completed days per level' is a scan; idx_tasks_type helps the GROUP BY. Migration 0086 (drizzle/migrations/0086_invoice_pay_link_and_terms.sql) is invoices.stripe_hosted_invoice_url + organisations.payment_terms and adds no task index.

Client-level grounding on organisations (db/schema.ts:28-99): planType ('maintain'|'scale'|'tune'|'launch'|'hourly'|'custom'|'none') :38; status :36; healthStatus ('green'|'amber'|'red') :50; paymentTerms ('card'|'net_7'|'net_14'|'net_30') :64; invoiceChannel :71; size ('micro'..'enterprise') :78; industry :33; tracksMode ('auto'|'custom'|'off') + customSmallTracks + customLargeTracks :85-87; defaultHourlyRate :76. Indexed on status, plan_type, stripe_customer_id, clerk_org_id.

Cadence and capacity grounding: subscriptions (db/schema.ts:370-402) carries planType, status, currentPeriodStart/End, hasPrioritySupport, billingInterval ('monthly'|'quarterly'|'annual'), includedAddons JSON. tracks (:405-420) carries type ('small'|'large'), isPriorityTrack, currentRequestId. lib/plan-utils.ts:22-48 getTrackEntitlements() derives smallTracks/largeTracks/totalSlots/canUseLargeTrack from planType + hasPrioritySupport and already gates the dialog's Size control (components/tahi/new-request-dialog.tsx:395-398).

Team capacity grounding: teamMembers.weeklyCapacityHours real default 40 (db/schema.ts:191), skills JSON (:196), roles JSON (:204), isContractor (:197), title/role (:189-190). GET /api/admin/reports/utilization?weeks=4 computes per-member utilisation as SUM(timeEntries.hours WHERE billable=1 AND date >= cutoff) / (weeklyCapacityHours * weeks), grouped in one query at app/api/admin/reports/utilization/route.ts:70-78, with green>=70 / amber>=50 / red thresholds. That is a usable assignee-load signal.

Actual-vs-estimate grounding exists via timeEntries (db/schema.ts:806-834): hours real NOT NULL, orgId, requestId (set null on delete), taskId, teamMemberId, date, billable, source ('manual'|'live_timer'|'imported'). Indexed on org_id, team_member_id, request_id, task_id. Joining timeEntries to delivered requests gives real hours per category per client, a stronger estimatedHours predictor than the nullable estimatedHours column.

Do NOT use /api/admin/reports/response-time as a signal. Its avgResponseMinutes is literally `Math.floor(Math.random() * 120 + 10)` (app/api/admin/reports/response-time/route.ts:33), with a comment admitting the simplification.

Two competing assignee models exist and a prediction must pick one: the scalar requests.assigneeId (db/schema.ts:443) and the requestParticipants junction with role 'pm' | 'assignee' | 'follower' (db/schema.ts:508-535, indexed on request_id, (participant_id, participant_type) and role, soft-deleted via removedAt). Historical 'who usually takes this category for this client' is cleanest off requestParticipants where role='assignee' AND removedAt IS NULL.

MCP parity (CLAUDE.md rule 14) already covers the neighbours: workers/mcp-server/src/index.ts exposes ai_triage_request (:1491, routed at workers/mcp-server/src/request-tools.ts:196-197), ai_request_wizard (:1487) and ai_task_wizard (:1482). A new suggestion endpoint needs a matching worker tool. The local mcp-server/ is dormant and must not be extended.

Sub-requests are a second create path with its own field set: the dialog posts to the sub-requests endpoint with `size` rather than `type` (components/tahi/new-request-dialog.tsx:548-553), so any autofill has to emit both vocabularies. requests.parentRequestId (db/schema.ts:449) and subPosition (:452) define the nesting; a sub-request inheriting its parent's dueDate and category is a zero-cost prediction needing no statistics.
risks: The cohort is probably empty for most clients. Memory project_pipeline_data_disposable records that tasks and requests are DEMO data, freely wiped during polish laps, while only pipeline, clients, contacts, invoices, finance and docs are real. A median over the last 90 days of a client's delivered requests may be computed from fabricated rows and read as authority. I did not query the live D1 (read-only, no browser), so actual per-org per-category row counts are unverified. Set a minimum cohort size (5 is the smallest number where a median means anything) and return no suggestion below it, the way lib/calculator/compute.ts:180 returns 'no_benchmark'.

requests.estimatedHours is nullable and NO create path writes it unless a human types it (app/api/admin/requests/route.ts:250 writes `estimatedHours ?? null`; same at app/api/admin/tasks/route.ts:321). Grounding an estimate prediction on that column risks a self-referential loop where the suggestion trains on earlier accepted suggestions. Grounding on SUM(timeEntries.hours) for delivered work is the honest signal, and it is what the utilisation report already uses.

The dialog's existing today+7 due date (components/tahi/new-request-dialog.tsx:201, :382) collides with the new feature. It is an ungrounded value presented as a real one, so 'the field is empty' is currently never true for due date on a request. Either that default is removed as part of this work or the new suggestion has nothing to fill and the two rules fight.

Requests can only store priority 'standard' or 'high' (lib/request-vocabulary.ts:54) but POST /api/admin/requests does not validate it (:247 writes it raw). The dead ai/suggest route already emits 'urgent' (app/api/admin/ai/suggest/route.ts:45). Any autofill reusing the task priority scale, or the wizard's low/medium/high/urgent scale, writes an unstorable value that the PATCH later rejects with a 400 the operator cannot explain.

A prediction firing on the CLIENT PORTAL create path is a client-visible claim about turnaround.
